The daily field guide for digital media

AI Media Scout

2026-11-26 · All platforms · Open-source software

The edition has 122 complete guides and 10 screened discoveries. It completes 29 earlier pending guides and details 2 substantive release updates. This edition follows local interview review on Windows and macOS, reference color across shots, editable drum notation and model-assisted tape restoration. The application, weights and media limits are recorded per workflow. Scarlet fixes speaker attribution during transcript corrections and adds a recovery route for export. LocalSR fixes output timestamps and launch issues on macOS 14 and 15. Godot extensions cover live transcription and baked mouth cues. AutoAOV offers per-pass neural denoising with documented limits on depth and motion data. A GitLab transcription prototype and an earlier SourceHut diffusion runner show how hosted recognition and local build dependencies affect the available workflow. Code grants were read in full. Models, services, creative inputs and hardware or software hosts have separate requirements. This edition is based on source review and published documentation. No discovered app was installed or run. The expanded plan covered 63 fields, 399/399 repository-query attempts and 23 model tasks. The repository lane recorded 398 successful, 1 partial and 0 failed queries, with 99 bounded. The model lane recorded 0 failed tasks. Metadata from 533 saved repository pages included 19,204 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog spans 125,439 candidates, including pilot history and 1,062 previously screened guides still pending before this edition. Creative relevance and the complete software grant were checked before including any discovery. Unreviewed and excluded records stay in local research. Live primary research yielded 471 complete usable responses from 567 distinct URL attempts, including a non-GitHub source in each of 63 fields. 3 captures reached the size bound and 93 other sources were inaccessible or unusable. The ecosystem checks cover all 8 configured groups and record available findings and gaps. Evidence labels in this edition are 0 Recommended, 0 Ready to try, 118 Quality unverified, 14 Experimental. Independent use remains unverified for 129 entries. The creative result check remains unverified for 130, and model, service or cost requirements remain unverified for 132. Repository searches returned no saved rows for Learned film, tape and audio restoration, Embodied and tactile interactive art, Multiband art and heritage imaging, Narrated and tactile exhibition interfaces, Learned shot matching and grading. Primary web research for these fields is included in the coverage notes. Updated evidence labels for previous entries: Diffuser (SourceHut) (Quality unverified to Experimental), Arabic Calligraphy for AI Agents (Quality unverified to Experimental), Arclight (Quality unverified to Experimental). 23 model tasks reached the configured response limit of 50 rows. A model record remains a discovery lead until code and use are verified. All saved model-task results were screened as metadata, covering 1,150 rows and 1,150 distinct model identities. The two linked source guides for the vocal denoiser and RCDL have separately verified software grants. The separate watchlist made 69 unsuccessful repository checks. Collection logged 1 enrichment failures. Credential-shaped material in unsealed captures was removed before sealing. The affected source origins and before-and-after hashes remain in private evidence.

Search and review counts

63 creative fields; 399/399 repository queries attempted; 23/23 model-task queries attempted. 21545 distinct source candidates and 1080 model leads. 122 detailed profiles and 10 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 1 partial repository queries, 99 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

Profiles are based on current primary documentation. Creative quality and performance claims are attributed to the developers unless hands-on testing is explicitly recorded. Unknown hardware requirements stay unknown. Code, model weights, hosted services, and required proprietary hosts can have different terms.

Today’s field coverage

FieldFinding
Images & designInvoke describes an editable image canvas with region-based generation. The image-to-image task documentation distinguishes transformation of an input image from generation using a text prompt alone. Split image-to-image inference from the layer or canvas editing interface. Save the source, output and model choice so a later color or composition pass is reproducible. 4 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Video, animation & filmThe LibreAIFrames publisher shows RIFE frame interpolation with scene-cut handling. FilmCraft publishes a separate nonlinear timeline whose native speech route has its own dependencies. Frame interpolation and timeline editing solve different stages. Compare generated inbetweens over a hard cut and retain the original timing. 3 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Audio, music & voiceThe Faust project documents routing and signal-processing integrations. The audio-to-audio model task lists learned transforms such as source separation and enhancement. An audio-to-audio model can transform an existing track while the DSP layer handles routing. Keep processed and dry stems aligned for comparison. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
3D, reconstruction & assetsThe Gaussian splatting authors optimize a representation from photographed views for novel-view rendering. FreeCAD documents a solid-model handoff that requires reconstructing editable geometry. A learned view-synthesis representation and editable parametric solids serve different downstream tasks. Preserve separate scene captures and design solids. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Browser tools & web mediaMediaPipe documents image, video and live-stream hand-landmark modes for web JavaScript. MDN describes the separate WebGPU adapter and device interfaces. The web hand-landmark guide documents client inference inputs and outputs. The WebGPU specification surface depends on browser and device support. Source 1 Source 2
WebXR, VR & ARThe Immersive Web material documents runtime access to headset input and display. Depth model documentation describes the map that can supply a separate stereo reconstruction stage. Separate the immersive rendering and interaction interface from the model used to produce or interpret an asset. Verify the actual browser and headset route. 3 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Computational art & creative codingMediaPipe’s browser hand landmarker exposes normalized landmark coordinates. Those coordinates can be read by a creative patch without handing the model control of the renderer. Hand landmark coordinates can drive a creative coding sketch. Calibrate input coordinate scaling and hold a recoverable neutral state when tracking drops. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2
Interactive, immersive & live mediaField 4’s example exposes learned speech embeddings as data available to a live audio and image patch. A live patch can map learned speech representations to scene controls. Test the mapping with likely performers and keep an editable scene. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
3D printing & generative CADFabDreamer’s authors describe semantic mask selection and layered design edits for laser-cut artwork. FreeCAD documents an independent route for measurable fabricated parts. Review generated parametric dimensions and geometry in a solid modeler before any physical cut or print. 2 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Games & production pipelinesThe audio-generation task supplies candidate game sounds. Godot’s WAV resource documents loop endpoints and playback settings for using those assets in the engine. Generated clips still need looping, trim and import checks inside the game engine. Keep editable sound sources and engine-ready copies. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1
Motion capture & character animationMediaPipe’s pose-landmarker guide describes image and world landmarks. CozyClay materials provide a separate, editable character and camera staging workflow. Pose inference and animation authoring generate different intermediate data. Check rotation, contact and frame cadence before retargeting. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Avatars, digital humans & lip syncThe Blender extension registry documents generating facial keys from spoken phonemes, with language-specific Vosk model selection in a separate dependency. The Blender lip-sync extension uses Vosk speech models and can produce editable keys. Select the model for the dialogue language and inspect consonants after baking. Source 1 Source 2
VFX, compositing & relightingThe light-aware compositing authors describe carrying image-dependent lighting into a composite. The related capture literature scopes where learned geometric estimates come from. Lighting-aware compositing and coarse learned geometry require shot-specific checks. Keep separate lighting, matte and source layers for revision. Source 1 Source 2
Spatial audio & volumetric mediaFAST-RIR’s authors model a diffuse room response conditioned on acoustic inputs. Open Spatial Delay documents a different layer, applying spatial routing and channel handling in a plugin. Scene-conditioned audio generation still needs a spatial routing stage. Verify the channel convention and playback decoder separately. 2 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Photogrammetry, scanning & neural renderingINRIA’s Gaussian splatting project provides the camera-view training method. The Blender developer notes discuss the data and rendering stages needed to bring splats into an editor. Neural view synthesis depends on a set of consistent views. Keep original cameras and an interchange copy of the learned scene. Source 1 Source 2
Editing, captions & post-productionThe OpenTimelineIO project documents a representation of clips, gaps and time. A video assistant that proposes cuts still needs an explicit mapping from these decisions to editor media and timing. Agent-directed edits need a transferable timeline. Reopen cuts in the finishing editor to check source-media relinking and timebase. Source 1 Source 2
Vector graphics, illustration & texturesThe SVG specification defines paths, coordinates and presentation attributes. SVGRender’s model materials are evidence for a separate learned vector-generation step. Vector model output can contain difficult paths or raster layers. Inspect editable curves, fill orientation and text before print export. Source 1 Source 2
Typography, fonts & layoutCounterpunch documents an optional assistant inside a glyph editor. FontForge documents editable glyph and font data for comparing what the assistant produces. The assistant in a font editor can aid glyph scripting. Maintain editable font sources and check spacing, script coverage and extrema. Source 1 Source 2
Storyboarding, narrative & comicsThe Drama AI project’s creative scope includes scene planning. CozyClay documents a stage where blocking and camera choices stay revisable. Separate scene planning from final renders. A creator can retain shots, actor blocking and source prompts as editable decisions. Source 1 Source 2
Creative publishing & presentationThe document-parser package describes structured extraction from source pages. The local caption package exposes the separate speech-timing route for editorial media. Structure extraction and speech timestamps can support editorial handoff. Proof reading order and text identity before publication. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Photography, restoration & colorPelli and FormDAM describe distinct parts of a shoot review, automated selection and semantic retrieval. The original ratings and camera files remain the reference for checking both. Photo culling and semantic search belong at different points in the selection workflow. Keep original RAW files and inspect selected and rejected frames. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Data art & scientific visualizationThe cited research and the MIT Media Lab’s Illuminate materials provide two places to check how data can become a visible mapping in a designed experience. When learned data supplies an art visualization, retain the raw observations and state how the model transforms the visual encoding. Source 1 Source 2
Physical, robotic & kinetic installationsThe MIT Media Lab publishes an example of sensing in a physical installation. The hand-landmarker guide provides a specific learned sensor output available for patching. Contact-free sensing can feed physical or projected media. Rehearse latency, lighting and the fallback behavior with the actual installation. Source 1 Source 2
Performance, projection & stage mediaThe IRCAM project documents using learned musical agents during composition and improvisation. Field 4 exposes speech embedding data to a separate performance patch. Map learned audio features to separate live cues and record a rehearsal trace before relying on the mapping on stage. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Fashion, textiles & wearable mediaThe OpenTryOn authors document garment-conditioned image synthesis. Editable measurements and garment templates live in a separate pattern authoring environment. Try-on synthesis previews a look. Pattern pieces, dimensions and physical fit require their own editable artifacts and validation. Source 1 Source 2
Accessible media & assistive creationW3C documents when a video needs descriptions of visual action. The linked publisher caption workflow produces dialogue text with a separate human review requirement. Automatic speech captions and descriptive narration cover different information needs. Review timed text and relevant visual events separately. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2
Mobile, edge & on-device creationF-Droid exposes an app distribution scoped to phone-side audio processing. The Android MediaPipe guide shows that model setup is its own mobile dependency. A phone-side workflow depends on device-specific model and media support. Check storage, export and offline behavior on the chosen device. Source 1 Source 2
Creative learning & authoringManim Voiceover documents interchangeable speech services that can be used while keeping classroom animation in an editable scene. Maintain scene scripts and narration timing as teaching assets. A speech service and a 3D learning project carry separate deployment requirements. Source 1 Source 2
Archives, media restoration & collectionsArkindex and eScriptorium describe document regions and transcription as data aligned with digitized source pages. Both prompt preserving the underlying facsimile. Transcribe digitized texts into a separately editable layer. Retain originals and record the OCR and reading-order corrections. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1 Source 2
Emerging & cross-disciplinary creative AIThe image-text-to-text task describes a model accepting mixed image and language inputs. That interface can support tagged asset review with a retained image-to-comment link. Model-assisted nodes can connect image, text and audio operations. Keep enough intermediate state to review and replace each dependency. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1
Hand-drawn and cutout animation inbetweensThe ToonCrafter authors and LibreAIFrames publisher show learned tools for making new frames from given drawings or video. Their examples use distinct input and timing assumptions. RIFE-style interpolation and learned cartoon inbetweens are distinct routes. Compare held frames, large pose changes and line stability on a short cel sequence. Source 1 Source 2
Layered illustration and cutout riggingLive2D documents editable cutout hierarchies. A separate pose landmarker provides observations a rigging workflow could map to selected controls. Keep the layered artwork and the rig separate when learned pose or interpolation drives a cutout. Maintain a reference pose for re-alignment. Source 1 Source 2
Comic lettering and editable panelsThe Japanese manga OCR project describes recognition inside dialogue crops. Keeping the source crop associated with the recognized line makes relettering reviewable. OCR can extract dialogue from panels for lettering. Verify reading order and characters before replacing original balloon artwork. 1 direct source attempts for this field were unavailable, bounded or unusable. Source 1
Multiband art and heritage imagingThe MIRA author documents aligning multiband heritage photography. Its registration step can be paired with a separately documented learned transcription layer when a source contains writing. MIRA documents multiband registration for heritage photography. Its development process alone does not establish end-user AI inference. Preserve registration references when pairing scans with learned transcription. Source 1 Source 2
Spatial soundfield reconstructionThe cited spatial plugin and authors’ room-response research establish different points of a route from estimated acoustic response to Ambisonic or binaural audition. The spatial plugin documents ambisonic and binaural output routes. Neural generation upstream and decoder compatibility downstream require independent checks. Source 1 Source 2
Scene-aware sound design and game audioSoundSpaces documents geometrical simulation of acoustics. Scene2Sound presents a learned approach to assigning sound to visual scene objects. Scene-conditioned sound design can use learned generation or spatial simulation. Keep coordinates and generated audio as separate authoring controls. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Live digital puppetry and stage charactersThe Blender extension registry describes phoneme animation. The web hand-landmarker guide describes a separate control signal for expressive puppets. Landmark and speech-driven workflows produce different puppet controls. Verify behavior during occlusion and silence before live use. Source 1 Source 2 Source 3
Multi-camera performance captureFreeMoCap’s maintainer documentation describes processing synchronized multi-camera recordings. Its context makes calibration and downstream retargeting explicit. Multi-camera pose capture depends on calibration and visible actors. Keep camera and skeleton data for checking retargeted movement. Source 1 Source 2
Editable rough cuts and media interchangeRelo presents an agent-directed video assembly workflow. OpenTimelineIO supplies a documented interchange target against which to check time and source links. Store model-assisted cut decisions on an editable timeline with original clips. Verify handles, timebase and relinking after the first export. Source 1 Source 2
Field recording and archival audio taggingCornell and the companion package document learned bird-call identification and timestamps, which a sound artist can use as an index into source recordings. Learned acoustic labels can index long field recordings. Keep confidence and offsets and review rare events against the original clip. Source 1 Source 2
Museum access and exhibition authoringZKM’s Beyond Matter release describes mixed exhibition contexts. W3C’s description guidance gives a separate specification for the accessible media inside an exhibit. ZKM documents a hybrid exhibit staging workflow. W3C describes separate visual description choices. An editable exhibition needs source records and accessible narration. Source 1 Source 2
AI-assisted contact sheets and photography proofingFormDAM documents searchable photo collections. Pelli presents a culling workflow that can be evaluated on a fixed copy of an existing shoot. Model-assisted proofing ranks or retrieves photos. Review decisions on a copy of the shoot and keep the original catalog and ratings available. Source 1 Source 2
Vector cleanup and printmaking preparationSVG’s path and transform rules give an editable target for a learned segmentation or vectorization stage. Record which shapes remain raster before preparing a print plate. Inspect a learned vector result at output size. Check path continuity, fills and lettering before splitting the art into separations. Source 1 Source 2
Costume patterns and garment prototypingOpenTryOn exposes learned visualization of garments on people. Seamly provides a documented stage for construction outlines and measurements. Keep authored measurements separate from generated try-on previews. Fit and sewing allowances depend on the editable pattern. Source 1 Source 2
Studio fabrication, surfaces and editable CAD3DCraft’s examples show a model-assisted route to parametric shape creation. ParCAD documents a separately editable solid model. Use measurable parametric outputs as the handoff from model-assisted form ideas. Validate unit, fit and toolchain before fabrication. Source 1 Source 2

Research beyond GitHub

  • gitlab · searched: Nine current search terms returned one page each. Eight reached the requested 20-row bound and video anonymization found one project. Its README redirects to the current deface upstream. The Nifty Little Tools Transcriber repository provided its complete AGPL grant and documents sending recordings to Google for transcription. The independent OpenDub source published v1.0.5, already represented in the library. Source Source Source Source Source
  • codeberg · searched: Six generic API searches returned HTTP 429. Direct source inspection still confirmed the current Facetracker license and release and returned ASR Subtitles documentation. No material update from either current source was established. Source Source Source
  • sourcehut · searched: Five targeted directory searches returned public pages. The diffusion results include a Stable Diffusion web demo and a Rust diffuser dependency. Creative AI produced no matching projects in its returned page. The earlier screened Diffuser entry has a complete MIT grant and a documented text-to-image route. Its current Cargo file points to a local checkout that makes the build path incomplete for a fresh user. The other targeted web demo did not yield a verifiable source grant. Source Source Source Source
  • packages · searched: DrumScript and Basic Pitch published package metadata and distributions with recoverable complete grants. Archive hashes were checked before reading the bundled license. The two projects document MusicXML engraving and audio-to-MIDI respectively. Source Source Source
  • creative-plugins · searched: The Blender registry documents a Vosk-driven lip-sync extension. The checksum-verified AutoAOV package declares its GPL-3.0-or-later grant and adds Blender compositor denoising for selected image passes. PopClip documents a distinct macOS extension host, and OBS documents the WebSocket route used by creative software integrations. Flathub’s targeted Sonist listing was unavailable from this research client. Source Source Source Source
  • project-sites · searched: CupCat and AICW Video publishers describe separate Windows and macOS interview review workflows. The SuperSplat project site provides an editable splat handoff for a different capture workflow. Source Source Source
  • research-code · searched: FabDreamer’s authors show learned masking in the laser-cut artwork workflow. FAST-RIR’s authors report conditioned acoustic responses and a speech evaluation. GEN3C’s authors publish camera-controlled generation examples, with separate software and model terms. Source Source Source
  • international · searched: Chinese OpenScreen and PymSS documentation contextualizes local captions and creator speech editing. The multilingual Whisper model card describes the separation of transcription and translation tasks. The profiles state platform requirements and export behavior at the workflow level. A coding agent uses the supplied project and creative instructions to author editable beat-aligned scenes. The canvas and FFmpeg pipeline deterministically render the resulting timing and layout. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Build a short kinetic music visual made of separate slide-like scenes, keeping the beat grid and visual code available for revision. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The Chinese documentation identifies a bundled synthetic loop, editable scene scaffold, browser preview and frame export commands. [1] [3]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [3]

  1. Read the documented agent skill scope before adding it to a project.
  2. Use its separate example scaffold with Node, a compatible browser, Python and FFmpeg as documented.
  3. Keep all audio and visual inputs local until you choose an authorized model route.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3]

  1. Prepare a permitted audio file and check its beat grid.
  2. Have a compatible coding agent draft a small set of scenes using the source constraints, then edit the layout and timing.
  3. Preview the sequence and verify output audio channel count and sync before keeping the export.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [3]

Hardware
Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.
Software
Node/Playwright Core, system Chrome/Edge, Python and FFmpeg for the documented canvas export. Model-based authoring uses a separate coding agent.
Platforms
Browser preview and source rendering route. The publisher documents a Windows FFmpeg path adjustment. Other setups are not separately validated.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1] [3]

  • Weights: MIT scaffold and code. Agent, song, graphics and fonts retain separate rights.
  • Commercial: Project code is governed by MIT. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
  • Cost: Local render and storage. Agent use and purchased media have independent terms.

Why it merits attention

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [3]

Limitations

A beat grid can miss tempo change and the project warns that export may appear correct with downmixed audio. Verify the actual output format. [1] [3]

Introduction

Transformers.js nodes make local image captions, object detections and embeddings available as signals in editable audio, video and hardware flows. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Prototype an artwork where a live camera’s recognized scene elements control a visual layer or display caption, while keeping the node graph editable. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The publisher documents a visual flow with a local model manager, a scene viewer and separate previews of audio and texture data. [1] [3]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [3]

  1. Choose the modern browser route or the exact documented Electron build for your device.
  2. For source use Node.js 20 or newer with npm/yarn. In the model manager preload one supported model before wiring its node.
  3. Check the release’s assets before assuming a platform package exists.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3]

  1. Create a small graph with one supported image input and a caption or detection node.
  2. Inspect the resulting fields before connecting them to your graphic control.
  3. Save the flow and test its behavior when the model, camera or output device is disconnected.

Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.

Browser or Electron plus local Transformers.js assets. The source build lists Node.js 20+. Hardware features have separate browser and CLASP support requirements.

Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge browser workflow is documented. Desktop docs name Windows, Linux and macOS. The v1.5.0 notes say macOS builds will follow that release.

Compare several enhancement passes over a small shot while retaining the original timing, crop and settings. [1] [3] [4] [5]

The publisher documents choosing a model, running previews before export and comparing output against the original. It publishes separate backend matrices per OS. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Choose the appropriate Windows release or Linux testing AppImage.
  2. Check host packages and GPU compatibility for the selected backend.
  3. Review what the first-run setup downloads and which private environment holds model and plugin files.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Open a short archival excerpt and record frame size and cadence.
  2. Compare output from a single qualified model using the same crop and timing.
  3. Validate skin, outlines and texture in motion before processing the rest of the archive.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [3]

  1. Run a short labeled audio segment and compare its MIDI against the recording.

  3. Save the project, then export MIDI or MusicXML and inspect the result in the receiving notation editor.
